author: Jocko Willink
quotes: Discipline gives you options that impulse will eventually take away.
Own the failure before asking anyone else to correct theirs.
A leader absorbs responsibility and distributes credit.
Calm thinking is a weapon when confusion enters the room.
The mission improves when the ego stops demanding protection.
Do the necessary work before your emotions begin voting on it.
When the plan breaks, adapt quickly and complain slowly.
You cannot lead people beyond standards you refuse to meet yourself.
Preparation reduces the number of decisions fear gets to make.
Every excuse surrendered is another piece of control regained.
Humility keeps a strong team from becoming a fragile one.
Responsibility is heavy, but helplessness weighs far more.
A difficult problem becomes smaller when everyone owns a piece of it.
Do not confuse aggression with leadership or silence with weakness.
The best response to failure is an honest review followed by action.
Lead yourself before requesting authority over anyone else.
Trust is earned through consistency when conditions become inconvenient.
The disciplined choice rarely asks whether you are in the mood.
When everything feels urgent, step back and identify what actually matters.
Give people clear direction, then give them room to execute.
Strong leaders make themselves useful rather than important.
The standard you tolerate becomes the standard you authorize.
Solve the problem without becoming another part of it.
Your response remains yours even when the situation is not.
Begin with the next controllable action and move forward from there.
